title: Korean Elementary Curriculum Learning Ontology controlled vocabulary

classes.definition: A versioned publication boundary that groups learning-map resources, release status, coverage gaps, and rights metadata.
A named and versioned educational programme whose standards and organizing structure apply to a stated jurisdiction and school level.
A controlled grouping of school grades used as the intended learning span for curriculum resources.
A curriculum-recognized field of study such as Korean Language, Mathematics, or Science.
An organizing area within a subject or curriculum, such as Reading or Number and Operations.
A source-anchored curriculum expectation identified by an official or repository-maintained standard code.
nonExamples: A verbatim official passage without an identifier

classes.definition: A repository-authored, teachable unit of learning aligned to one or more achievement standards.
A navigational grouping that contains one or more learning topics under a documented coverage policy.
A learner-observable condition used to judge whether a learning topic has been demonstrated.
nonExamples: A teacher activity with no learner evidence

classes.definition: A prompt or task that elicits evidence relevant to a learning topic.
A document or repository artifact cited as evidence for curriculum identity, codes, mappings, or provenance.
nonExamples: A rights permission not recorded for the document

classes.definition: A structured location inside or alongside a source document, including page, section, attachment, hash, or code anchors.
nonExamples: A source URL with no item-level location

classes.definition: A dated or status-bearing record of what was checked, by which method, and with what limitations.
nonExamples: An unqualified claim of official approval

classes.definition: An explicit source-data completeness, calibration, reconciliation, or review gap retained for release evaluation.
nonExamples: The absence of an RDF serialization in P0

classes.definition: An n-ary record that qualifies a model-relative direct prerequisite suggestion with strength, reason, basis, source, and review state.
nonExamples: An absolute universal law about learning order

classes.definition: An n-ary record that qualifies how a learning topic relates to an achievement standard, preserving alignment kind, confidence, note, basis, and source.
nonExamples: A statement that the topic reproduces official standard text

objectProperties.definition: Associates a dataset release with a curriculum included in that release.
Associates a curriculum or learning resource with its subject.
Associates a curriculum resource with its intended grade band.
Associates a subject-scoped learning resource with its organizing learning domain.
Lists an achievement standard governed by a curriculum.
Lists a learning topic published in a dataset release.
Lists a learning cluster published in a dataset release.
Places a learning topic in a navigational learning cluster.
Provides a convenient navigation edge from a topic to a standard when a StandardTopicAlignment record retains the qualifiers.
Links a learning topic to its qualifier-preserving standard alignment record.
Identifies the learning topic qualified by a standard-topic alignment record.
Identifies the achievement standard qualified by a standard-topic alignment record.
Associates a learning topic with learner-observable evidence criteria.
Associates a learning topic with a prompt intended to elicit evidence.
States a reviewed, model-relative suggested direct prerequisite edge; it is never an absolute universal fact about learning order.
Indicates that a prerequisite is reachable through two or more directRequires edges and is therefore a derived navigation relation.
Provides the derived inverse navigation direction of directRequires.
Links a dependent learning topic to the qualifier-preserving record for one direct prerequisite suggestion.
Identifies the topic whose suggested prerequisite is qualified by a prerequisite assertion.
Identifies the suggested direct prerequisite qualified by a prerequisite assertion.
Associates a curriculum resource or assertion with a source document that supports its identity, provenance, or basis.
Associates a source-backed resource with a structured source locator.
Associates a resource or qualified assertion with a record of its verification status and limitations.
Associates a dataset release with a retained source-data coverage or review gap.

datatypeProperties.definition: The stable source or repository identifier for a resource.
The preferred human-readable label in a declared language.
A repository-authored concise description that does not reproduce official text unless explicitly licensed and marked.
The recorded date on which a source document was accessed.
The repository attachment number retained for a source document.
The country code for the dataset release.
A repository-authored description of a learning topic.
The canonical source generation timestamp retained as source metadata.
The documented workstream basis used to generate a learning topic.
An English-language label retained alongside the preferred Korean label.
The locale identifier for the dataset release.
A parent-facing summary for a learning cluster.
A source-document PDF page count or page value retained by the canonical source record.
The publisher named by a source document record.
The school level governed by a curriculum.
The bounded source basis recorded for an achievement standard.
A human-readable section label retained for an achievement standard.
The source achievement-standard code retained by a learning topic.
The canonical source-document type token.
The official or repository-maintained achievement-standard code.
A source status token retained for a dataset release or coverage gap.
The external subject code retained by a source document.
An English-language title for a topic or cluster.
The bounded verification limitations retained for an achievement standard.
The curriculum version label.
The repository workstream file associated with a generated resource.
A controlled LearningTopicType concept used for faceted navigation rather than an asserted disjoint class.
The inclusive lower age hint carried by a learning topic.
The inclusive upper age hint carried by a learning topic.
The learner-observable statement expressed by an evidence criterion.
The task wording expressed by an assessment prompt.
The required or recommended qualifier for a direct prerequisite assertion.
A human-readable explanation for a suggested direct prerequisite.
The exact hard or soft source token retained alongside its normalized prerequisite strength.
The method, workstream, or evidence basis used to create a qualified assertion.
A source identifier or repository path retained with a qualified assertion.
The introduces, supports, extends, or assesses role expressed by a standard-topic alignment.
A bounded 0 to 1 confidence score for a qualified assertion, never a substitute for its basis or source.
The exact alignment relationship token retained from the canonical mapping record.
The exact source confidence token retained separately from the numeric working confidence.
The exact optional note retained from the canonical alignment record.
The exact optional legacy rationale retained separately from an alignment note.
Whether numeric confidence came from the release default rather than a numeric source token.
The named release policy used when a numeric working value is defaulted.
The exact optional verification-status token retained from the canonical alignment record.
Whether the alignment verification record uses the release default because the source omitted a status.
An optional human-readable qualification or limitation on an assertion or verification record.
A retrieval URL recorded for a source document without implying dereference permanence or reuse permission.
A content hash used to identify a checked source artifact.
A page, printed page, attachment number, section, or source code value inside a structured source locator.
The controlled status of a verification record, including the limits of what was checked.
The controlled reuse and redistribution posture recorded for a source document or dataset release.
Whether official source wording is included in the described resource.
Whether the canonical coverage-gap record supplied an explicit severity before normalization.
The controlled source-data completeness or review category assigned to a coverage gap.
The controlled urgency or intentionality level assigned to a coverage gap.
A human-readable account of what is missing, intentionally excluded, or awaiting review.

conceptSchemes.definition: Facets describing the learning work emphasized by a topic; values may overlap and are not asserted as disjoint OWL classes.

concepts.definition: A topic emphasizing concepts, relationships, categories, or explanatory understanding.
A topic emphasizing comprehension or production through spoken, written, signed, or multimodal language.
A topic emphasizing reflection, strategy selection, self-monitoring, or evaluation of one's learning process.
A topic emphasizing an ordered method, performance routine, or repeatable course of action.
A topic emphasizing the interpretation or construction of diagrams, symbols, models, notation, or other representations.

conceptSchemes.definition: Strength of a reviewed prerequisite recommendation, normalized without changing legacy source values.

concepts.definition: The released model recommends treating the direct prerequisite as required for its current learning path; this is not a universal learner claim.
The released model recommends the direct prerequisite while allowing an alternate sequence; this is not a universal learner claim.

conceptSchemes.definition: The pedagogical role a learning topic plays relative to an achievement standard.

concepts.definition: The topic establishes an initial entry point to the knowledge or performance expressed by the standard.
The topic contributes practice or understanding that supports the standard without being its sole focus.
The topic develops the standard beyond its initial scope or expected level.
The topic provides a context in which evidence relevant to the standard is elicited or evaluated.

conceptSchemes.definition: Categories for source-data completeness and review gaps; ontology-format phase status and rights posture are deliberately outside this scheme.

concepts.definition: A gap concerning whether and how source wording may be stored or reproduced.
A gap in item-level page, section, attachment, hash, code, or equivalent source location evidence.
A gap where an intended curriculum area, topic, or learning requirement is absent or incomplete.
A gap requiring review by a qualified subject, curriculum, pedagogy, or classroom expert.
A gap requiring calibration of evidence criteria, prompts, difficulty, or scoring interpretation.
A gap requiring review of prerequisite direction, strength, explanation, or graph placement.
A gap requiring conflicting, amended, duplicated, or versioned source records to be reconciled.

conceptSchemes.definition: Urgency or intentionality labels preserved for coverage gaps.

concepts.definition: The gap has high release or interpretation impact and should be prioritized.
The gap has material but bounded impact and should be scheduled for review.
The gap has limited current impact but remains explicitly tracked.
Severity has not been settled and requires a reviewer decision.
The recorded omission or limitation is deliberate under the current release policy.
The source record supplies no severity; the absence is preserved rather than inferred.

conceptSchemes.definition: Review states that describe what evidence was checked without implying official approval.

concepts.definition: A bounded source identity, code, or locator check was completed against the named official source; approval, verbatim inclusion, and rights clearance are not implied.
The record was derived from an identified public document under the stated text and rights limitations.
The record passed the repository's documented workstream review but has no implied external endorsement.
The record still requires a specified source or model verification action.
No bounded verification action is recorded for the resource.

conceptSchemes.definition: Reuse and redistribution posture kept separate from content coverage and ontology-format phase status.

concepts.definition: Reuse or redistribution is blocked pending work-level terms or permission evidence.
Documented evidence supports the stated reuse or redistribution scope.
The rights posture has not been determined and must not be treated as permission.
